status_summary: All three withdrawals had been completed before 2025, so the Mandate's conditional request is matched only by later reversals. For the Boundary Waters, the House (2026-01-21, 214 to 208) and Senate (2026-04-16, 50 to 49) passed H.J.Res. 140, which the President signed on 2026-04-27 as Public Law 119-85, disapproving the 20-year withdrawal of about 225,504 acres. For Chaco, BLM took comment through 2026-07-29 on an assessment proposing full revocation of the 336,404 acre buffer withdrawal, with no final decision found. No federal action on the Thompson Divide withdrawal (Public Land Order 7939, published 2024-04-08) was found, though a February 2025 report said it could be reconsidered. For the Boundary Waters leases, an Interior memo of 2025-07-17 reinstated a Solicitor opinion favorable to the Twin Metals lease renewals.

timeline.event: The Interior Deputy Secretary, by memorandum to the Acting Solicitor, withdrew Solicitor Opinion M-37072 and reinstated M-37049, the earlier opinion supporting renewal of the Twin Metals mineral leases (MNES-01352 and MNES-01353) near the Boundary Waters, and directed all bureaus to treat M-37049 as binding; the memo does not itself reinstate or renew a lease.
House passed H.J.Res. 140, the Congressional Review Act resolution disapproving Public Land Order 7917 (Boundary Waters area withdrawal), 214 to 208.
Senate passed H.J.Res. 140 without amendment, 50 to 49 (roll call 84).
President signed H.J.Res. 140, which became Public Law 119-85, disapproving the 2023 order that withdrew about 225,504 acres in Cook, Lake and Saint Louis Counties, Minnesota, for 20 years.
BLM opened comment, through 2026-07-29, on an environmental assessment whose proposed action would fully revoke Public Land Order 7923, the Chaco buffer withdrawal of about 336,404 acres.

title: Reverse mineral withdrawals at Thompson Divide, Chaco and the Boundary Waters
uncertainties: The 'completed' reading of the withdrawals relies on the Chaco and Boundary Waters sources describing them as 20-year orders and on Public Land Order 7939 (Federal Register, 2024-04-08), which withdrew the Thompson Divide. Federal Register API queries on 2026-10-25 for Thompson Divide (since 2025-01-20), Chaco (since 2026-07-01) and Boundary Waters (since 2026-04-01) returned no Interior revocation, public land order or notice on any of the three after the dates already recorded, and the BLM Chaco page of 2026-07-15 gives no decision date. The 2025-07-17 Interior memo concerns the legal opinion governing the Twin Metals lease renewals; a news report says Interior moved to restore the leases, but no dated primary record of a lease reinstatement was found, so lease actions are not counted. The Minnesota executive order of 2026-08-18 rests only on a hoodline.com report, an aggregator treated as an unverified lead, so that source was removed on 2026-10-25; the state order itself was not read. Public Land Order 7939 (Thompson Divide, 2024-04-08) predates 2025-01-20 and is context only, not a timeline event.
